questions.question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Magnanimity
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 4)** Altruism**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnanimity** (उदारता)** **refers to the quality of being **generous, noble, and forgiving.** It is the act of being forgiving or generous in treating others, especially those who have wronged you.
 
• **Altruism **(परोपकारिता, परहितवाद)**,** on the other hand, refers to selfless concern for the welfare of others, even at the cost of one's own interests. Both words have a sense of generosity and selflessness, but altruism specifically refers to the act of putting others before oneself.

Therefore, **altruism** is the word that means the same as magnanimity. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virulence** refers to the ability of a pathogen to cause disease. (द्वेष)
 
• **Invidiousness** refers to the quality of being envious or resentful. (द्वेषपूर्णता)
 
• **Volatile** refers to something that is easily evaporated or changed. None of these words share the same meaning as magnanimity. ((स्थिति) जो अचानक और अप्रत्‍याशित रूप से बदल जाए)

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct passive form of the sentence.

Ravi gave you the information?

options.text: Was the information given to you by Ravi?
Have the information been given to you?
Has the information given to you?
You have been given the information?

questions.solution:
The correct passive form of the sentence is option **1) "Was the information given to you by Ravi?**" [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the active sentence "Ravi gave you the information," the subject "Ravi" performs the action on the object "you" and "the information."
 
• In the passive form, the object becomes the subject of the sentence, and the subject becomes the object.
 
• Here's an explanation of how the active sentence "Ravi gave you the information" is transformed into the passive form "Was the information given to you by Ravi?" using the rules for converting from active to passive voice:
 
• Identify the subject, verb, and object:
 
 
• Subject: Ravi
 
• Verb: gave
 
• Object: the information
 
 
 
• Move the object to the beginning of the sentence and make it the subject of the passive sentence:
 
 
• The information
 
 
 
• Use the appropriate form of the verb "be" (in this case, "was") followed by the past participle of the main verb (in this case, "given"):
 
 
• Was given
 
 
 
• Include the preposition "by" followed by the agent (the person or thing performing the action):
 
 
• By Ravi
 
 
 
• If there is an indirect object in the active sentence (in this case, "you"), include it after the preposition "to":
 
 
• To you
 
 
 
• Putting it all together, we get the passive form: "**Was the information given to you by Ravi?**"
 
 
• This passive sentence correctly conveys that the information was given by Ravi to you.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

However, even after Independence in 1947, British expatriate firms did not suddenly ___________ from India.
questions.solution:
"The correct answer is **option 3, "divest."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To divest** means** to sell off or get rid of something, often referring to a company or organization selling off assets or investments.**
 
• In the context of the sentence, it means that British expatriate firms did not suddenly sell off or get rid of their businesses in India after Independence in 1947.
 
 
• **Example:** The company decided to **divest **its non-core assets to focus on its main business.
 
 
 
• **Option 1, "close," **means to shut down or cease operations. In the context of the sentence, it would mean that British expatriate firms shut down their businesses in India after Independence.
 
 
• **Example**: The restaurant had to **close **due to a lack of customers.
 
 
 
• **Option 2, "disallow," **means to forbid or prohibit something. In the context of the sentence, it does not make sense as British expatriate firms were not forbidden or prohibited from operating in India after Independence.
 
 
• **Example**: The teacher **disallowed **the use of calculators during the exam.
 
 
 
• **Option 4, "consecrate,"** means to make something sacred or holy. In the context of the sentence, it does not make sense as British expatriate firms were not made sacred or holy in India after Independence.
 
 
• Example: The church was **consecrated **by the bishop.
 
 
 
• Overall, **option 3, "divest," **is the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *However, even after Independence in 1947, British expatriate firms did not suddenly __**divest**__ from India.*

• The sentence talks about the development of basic welfare services in former colonies such as Ghana, Jamaica, India, and the Philippines. The sentence is made up of four parts that need to be rearranged in the correct order to make sense.
 
• Let's look at each part of the sentence:
 
• **Q**. In former colonies, such as Ghana, Jamaica, India and the

• **S.** Philippines the basic welfare services grew out of modified
 
 
• This part of the sentence provides information about the basic welfare services in the Philippines and how they were developed.
 
 
 
• **P.** versions of the European poor laws, charitable and
 
 
• This part of the sentence talks about the European poor laws and charitable activities, which were likely sources of inspiration for the basic welfare services in former colonies.
 
 
 
• **R. **missionary activities, and the introduction of Western juvenile justice procedures
 
 
• This part of the sentence talks about the role of missionary activities and Western juvenile justice procedures in the development of basic welfare services in former colonies.
 
 
 
• Putting these parts of the sentence in order, we get: **QSPR**, which gives us the correct sentence structure and makes sense in the given context.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2) QSPR.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The sage said, “Man proposes and God disposes.”

options.text: The sage said that man proposes and God disposes.
The sage said that man propose and God dispose.
The sage said that man proposed and God disposed.
The sage said that man had proposed and God had disposed.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1: The sage said that man proposes and God disposes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When converting a sentence from** direct to indirect speech,** we need to make some changes to the original sentence.
 
• Here are the rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb (said) is changed to a reporting clause (that + subject + verb).
 
• The pronouns and possessive adjectives are changed to reflect the new subject of the sentence.
 
• The tense of the verb is usually shifted back one tense (present becomes past, past becomes past perfect).
 
• Time and place expressions may need to be changed.
 
 
 
• Using these rules, we can convert the given sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• **Direct speech:** The sage said, "Man proposes and God disposes."
 
• **Indirect speech:** The sage said that man proposes and God disposes.
 
• The given reported speech is a general truth, therefore, there will be no change in the tense of the reported speech.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 1.**
